title: Create meaningful tests
summary: Derive tests from acceptance criteria, then prove they catch a real defect, not just pass.

questions.text: Which behavior must the tests prove? Paste or point to the acceptance criteria.
questions.why: Tests derived from acceptance criteria catch real defects; tests derived from code only mirror it.

questions.text: Which failure and edge cases matter (invalid input, wrong password, empty, unauthorized)?
questions.why: Happy-path-only suites are the most common weakness of generated tests.

questions.text: What test data or fixtures should be used? (No production data or real credentials.)
questions.why: Isolated fixtures prevent flaky, order-dependent tests.

questions.text: How do you run the tests for this project?
questions.why: Tests that never ran prove nothing.

staged_actions.instruction: List test cases (happy, negative, boundary) mapped to each acceptance criterion. Wait for approval before writing code.
Write the tests in the project's existing framework and style. Assert observable behavior, not implementation details. No fixed sleeps, no real credentials.
Run {test_command} and paste the results. Then show that at least one test fails when the behavior is broken (for example against the known defect).

acceptance.text: Tests ran and the results were captured.
At least one test fails when the behavior is broken (detects the known defect).
No test passes only because it checks existence or type instead of behavior.
No secrets or credentials in test files or fixtures.

evidence_requirements: Test run output or JUnit XML report
teaching_tip: A test that passes on broken code proves nothing. Check that your tests fail when the behavior is wrong.

exercise.prompt: The smoke tests pass. Does that mean login works?
exercise.answer_hint: No. They pass even with the wrong-password defect, so they don't test the behavior.
